identity.name: DATA PATTERNS INDIA LTD
identity.industry: Defence electronics — radar/avionics/EW systems (in-house design, IP-driven)

summary.oneLiner: IP-led, debt-free indigenous defence-electronics house at the start of a multi-year scale-up: order inflows tripled in FY26 (+216% to ~INR1,121cr), order book ~INR2,062cr (incl. negotiated), plus a ~INR1,900cr pipeline of single-vendor repeat orders on already-delivered/accepted products that mgmt expects to convert over the next 12 months. Near-term guidance is a deliberately conservative 20–25% revenue CAGR at 38–40% EBITDA margins, net-cash, but mgmt repeatedly signalled it is targeting a "multi-thousand-crore" company and growth "substantially higher than guidance."
summary.business: Data Patterns (India) Limited designs, develops, manufactures and services electronic products for Defence and Aerospace customers, spanning Radar and Fire Control Systems, Avionics and Electronic Warfare, Automatic Test Equipment, and repair/overhaul/job-work services. It operates as a single reportable segment, serving predominantly Government and Public Sector Undertaking customers in India along with a small but growing export book.

currentContext.strengths: Strong reputation for delivering high-quality products and services in Defence and aerospace sectors|Robust domain capability in Radars, Electronic Warfare, Communication systems, Avionics & Satellite Systems|Significant, sustained investment in R&D allowing continuous innovation ahead of market trends|Strong internal quality process and quality team|Scalable business model with potential to build complete systems|Deep technical expertise in electronic systems design, embedded software development and manufacturing|Senior personnel associated with the Company for more than two decades, indicating institutional continuity|Philosophy of investing ahead of opportunities, so products are already developed and validated before programmes are launched by customers
currentContext.strategies: Invest ahead of opportunities — develop and validate products before customer programmes emerge, so the Company can participate meaningfully when defence modernisation opportunities open up|Continuously identify technology gaps and build indigenous solutions in areas where domestic alternatives are limited or unavailable, across radar systems, electronic warfare, communication systems, airborne platforms and strategic defence technologies|Expand addressable market through innovation, engineering excellence and in-house intellectual property creation rather than only participating in existing markets|Grow exports as a long-term strategic pillar, building on repeat UK business and expanding engagement across Europe and other international markets|Pushed 'Process Excellence' to the forefront — streamlining operations and reinforcing governance across all levels to enable responsible scale-up of infrastructure and capability|Elevate workforce capability through targeted upskilling and enhanced resource utilisation to support a leaner, more agile, high-performance organisation|Integrate ESG principles across expanding operations, from manufacturing eco-efficiency to community-focused CSR initiatives|Company operates a debt-free balance sheet and maintains an adequate cash balance to meet strategic objectives; it follows a formal Dividend Distribution Policy (available on the Company website) and has paid final dividends each year (Rs 7.90/share for FY25, Rs 10/share recommended for FY26), with no transfer to General Reserve made in FY26 as retained earnings are used to fund growth. Non-executive director remuneration is governed by criteria including Company performance, independence, contribution to Board discussions and participation in strategic decision-making, limited to sitting fees and profit-linked commission. The Company has no subsidiaries and does not prepare consolidated financial statements.
currentContext.expansion: FY26 was described by management as a year of 'historic, tangible expansions' in capability and infrastructure, following a year of vision-setting. The Company continued to build out its Siruseri, Chennai campus, including an EMI-EMC Testing Facility funded from QIP proceeds (against an object of Rs 15.23 Cr, Rs 13.63 Cr had been utilised and Rs 1.60 Cr remained unutilised as at March 31, 2026). QIP proceeds earmarked for product development (Rs 167.24 Cr object) had Rs 131.19 Cr utilised and Rs 36.05 Cr unutilised as at the same date, continuing investment in Radar, Electronic Warfare, Communication and Satellite product lines. Management also referenced 'upcoming infrastructure expansion' built on strengthened internal processes and governance to support the Company's next phase of growth, though no additional named site or capacity project beyond the EMI-EMC facility was disclosed in the routed text.
currentContext.mdna: Rising defence spending, increasing indigenisation, growing demand for advanced electronics and expanding global opportunities cited as key growth drivers going forward|Growing participation of private industry and increasing government defence allocations under Aatmanirbhar Bharat create what management calls a 'once-in-a-generation opportunity' for Indian defence technology companies|Order inflow growth attributed to diversified wins across multiple defence and aerospace programmes, reflecting growing customer confidence in the Company's technological capabilities and execution track record|Growing acceptance of the Company's capabilities in international markets, with increasing interest from customers outside India as global defence spending and armed-forces modernisation rise|Multiple in-house R&D programmes (electronic warfare suites incl. self-protection jammer pods, airborne surveillance radars, maritime applications, drone detection/counter-drone technologies, electronic support systems) have reached advanced stages of development and validation, positioned as the next phase of growth|All-time high order book in the Company's history as of FY26 year-end|Order inflows of approximately Rs 1,121 crore recorded during FY26, representing growth of 216% year-on-year, diversified across multiple defence and aerospace programmes|Export order book of approximately Rs 53 crore as on date, with continued repeat business from the United Kingdom and active engagement with customers across Europe and other international markets|Successful development, export and acceptance of the Transportable Precision Approach Radar (TPAR) by a European customer marked as an important export milestone

risks.risk: Heavy dependence on government/PSU customers and Defence spending
risks.note: Business heavily relies on government contracts, making it vulnerable to fluctuations in government spending and regulatory changes; majority of customers are Government or Public Sector Undertakings.
Company operates only in one segment — manufacture, sale and service of Defence electronics — with no reportable segment diversification, concentrating all revenue in one industry cycle.

risks.risk: Long development cycles and high upfront costs straining working capital
risks.note: The Defence industry involves high upfront costs and long development cycles which can strain financial resources and affect profitability; extensive gestation of development contracts may lead to strain on working capital, and working capital cycles were flagged as challenging.
Rapid advancements in technology could potentially render existing products and solutions obsolete if not continuously innovated upon, requiring sustained R&D investment to stay current.
Changes in government regulations, export controls, or compliance requirements could impact the Company's ability to operate and export its products.

risks.risk: Supply-chain dependence on external suppliers amid geopolitical instability
risks.note: Dependence on suppliers for critical components and materials exposes the Company to risks of raw-material shortages, transportation issues, or geopolitical instability, highlighted in the context of the Russia-Ukraine conflict and West Asia crisis; Company noted some delays in sourcing material from global sources though no outright supply failure, and continues evaluating mitigation.

thesis: IP-led, debt-free indigenous defence-electronics house at the start of a multi-year scale-up: order inflows tripled in FY26 (+216% to ~INR1,121cr), order book ~INR2,062cr (incl. negotiated), plus a ~INR1,900cr pipeline of single-vendor repeat orders on already-delivered/accepted products that mgmt expects to convert over the next 12 months. Near-term guidance is a deliberately conservative 20–25% revenue CAGR at 38–40% EBITDA margins, net-cash, but mgmt repeatedly signalled it is targeting a "multi-thousand-crore" company and growth "substantially higher than guidance."

Note: Q4 was 37% of FY26 revenue vs 55% in FY25 (less back-ended). Q4 margins flattered by 100% in-house full-system deliveries with no bought-out content.
guidance:
- Revenue growth ~20–25% over short term; mgmt believes actual will be "substantially higher" if repeat/export orders land early.
- EBITDA margin 38–40%; remain net cash / debt-free.
- Cash conversion cycle targeted to settle at ~320–340 days (from 365).
- Aspiration: build order book of ≥3 years' revenue for predictable growth; scale to multi-thousand-crore over 2–3 years.
order book:
- FY26 inflows ~INR1,121cr (+216% YoY), diversified across radar, avionics, EW, services, strategic electronics.
- Order book at Mar-2026 ~INR926cr; incl. negotiated/expected ~INR2,062cr.
- Negotiated bucket now ~INR1,090cr (multiple cases, some already converted), expected to be contracted in next 1–2 months; ~INR100cr of it is services, rest products → product order book heading to ~INR1,500cr+.
- Additional ~INR1,900cr of single-vendor repeat orders on already-delivered products expected to fructify within FY27 (timing not in company's control — govt customers).
- Export order book ~INR53cr (UK repeat business; precision approach radar exported to a European country with site acceptance).
- Services ~38% of current order book / ~INR350cr (AMC, multi-year; billed as performed, so no receivable build-up).
- Largest Q4 order: IMD radar development + service order (~18-month execution).
segment: Radar (airborne surveillance & fire-control, maritime, drone-detection), EW/ESM (self-protection jammer pods — competing with Germany, flight-testing next), avionics (glass cockpit + mission systems for LCA Mk2, feeding AMCA), communication/ComInt, IFF, missile seekers (BrahMos seeker first variant under execution; one air-defence seeker in delivery). Mix shifting toward complete in-house full systems (incl. software), which lifts margins.
growth: Drivers: indigenisation/import substitution, geopolitical defence-capex supercycle (domestic + Europe/UK/US/Japan/Korea exports), repeat orders on accepted products, new product repurposing (anti-drone detection/spoofing/jamming — quick, low-hanging), and seekers/airborne radar/EW programs. AMCA RFP expected "any time now."
margins: FY26 EBITDA 40% (gross 63%). Q4 spike (EBITDA 56%, gross 73%) driven by 100% in-house full-system deliveries with zero bought-out content; weaker quarters reflect strategic low-margin contracts taken deliberately to build full-system/PMO/mechanical capability. Mgmt warns against contract-by-contract margin extrapolation; structural guide is 38–40%.
capex: Aggressive but "judicious" capacity build: ~nine floors of new factory space; capacity for export contracts and seekers already built; infrastructure lead time 1–2 years so investing ahead of the scaling. Cautious not to overspend before contracts land. Product development largely expensed (not capitalised); ~1,200 engineers.
capital allocation: Debt-free, net-cash; no leverage taken. Cash deployed into R&D (expensed), capacity expansion and new-product development. No buyback/dividend commentary this call. Focus on improving working-capital cycle.
risks:
- Order timing entirely dependent on government/agency approval cycles (HAL, DRDO, MoD) — lumpy, unpredictable.
- Revenue back-ending / quarterly volatility (Q4 −13% YoY despite strong FY).
- Long working-capital cycle (365 days).
- Margin variability from strategic low-margin contracts.
- Execution/air-trial timelines for EW & new radars (1.5–2 yrs); BrahMos seeker production timing (mgmt downplays risk).
- DRDO gating of missile/seeker programs; capex stranded if contracts slip.
- Competition from foreign OEMs and domestic peers (e.g., Astra Microwave moving into systems).
mgmt tone: Highly bullish and expansive — MD explicitly gave a "first time all-rounded view" on market, investment and scaling, repeatedly stressing growth "substantially higher than guidance" and a multi-thousand-crore ambition. Defensive/irritable on analyst mischaracterisations (denied any "delays" or "poor execution"; insisted execution is fast and good, delays are government-side). Conservative on giving hard timelines/revenue for unproven programs.
non-obvious:
- "Virupaksha" radar (Super Sukhoi) is a DRDO project, NOT a Data Patterns product — mgmt corrected analyst; DPIL has its own equivalent it expects IAF to adopt later.
- Q4 high margin is a mix artifact (no bought-out), not a new run-rate.
- INR1,900cr repeat pipeline is OUTSIDE the INR2,062cr order book and OUTSIDE guidance — large optionality.
- EW self-protection jammer pods already received by IAF, poised for flight testing → medium-term revenue.
- Pursuing electro-optic seekers via an industry partner; wants to become an "electro-optics" not just electronics company.
- Services billed only as performed → does not inflate receivables despite rising services mix.

qoq change log:
First tracked file for DATAPATTNS (no prior summary in repo). Key Q4 FY26 / FY26 markers vs prior commentary referenced on call:
- Order inflow FY26 ~INR1,121cr, +216% YoY — step-change vs FY25.
- Negotiated-order bucket grew from ~INR1,000cr (prior call) to ~INR1,090cr; some converted; total order book now ~INR2,062cr.
- Q4 revenue −13% YoY but +99% QoQ; FY26 less back-ended (37% in Q4 vs 55% in FY25).
- Cash conversion cycle improved to 365 days (from 428); now targeting 320–340.
- New disclosures: ~INR1,900cr single-vendor repeat pipeline; EW jammer pods accepted by IAF and heading to flight test; AMCA RFP "any time now"; anti-drone product suite entering demos; nine-floor factory expansion underway.

themes.title: Defence indigenization & order-book visibility
themes.need: Indigenization mandates (IDDM / Atmanirbhar / DcPP) plus multi-year order books make domestic defence the cleanest revenue-conversion theme - across electronics, drones, simulators, explosives/munitions and precision systems. BEL guides >INR55k cr FY27 inflow (~INR30k cr QRSAM pending CCS clearance, guided by September) on a INR72,258cr order book; HAL book ~INR2.55 lakh cr; SOLARINDS defence revenue +94% to INR2,634cr FY26, guided >INR4,500cr FY27 on an ~INR18,000cr defence order book (Bhargavastra counter-drone trials completing CY2026); DATAPATTNS inflows strong; BHARATFORG/BEML add land-systems and platforms.
themes.driver: Backlog-to-revenue conversion underway; BEL's QRSAM CCS clearance (guided by Sep-2026, ~INR30k cr of the FY27 inflow guide) is the load-bearing near-term catalyst; fresh MoD orders + emergency procurement; HAL LCA Mk-1A ramp (gated on GE engines).

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Data Patterns (India) Limited designs, develops, manufactures and services electronic products for Defence and Aerospace customers, spanning Radar and Fire Control Systems, Avionics and Electronic Warfare, Automatic Test Equipment, and repair/overhaul/job-work services. It operates as a single reportable segment, serving predominantly Government and Public Sector Undertaking customers in India along with a small but growing export book.

segment_detail.title: Segment
segment_detail.body: Radar (airborne surveillance & fire-control, maritime, drone-detection), EW/ESM (self-protection jammer pods — competing with Germany, flight-testing next), avionics (glass cockpit + mission systems for LCA Mk2, feeding AMCA), communication/ComInt, IFF, missile seekers (BrahMos seeker first variant under execution; one air-defence seeker in delivery). Mix shifting toward complete in-house full systems (incl. software), which lifts margins.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Radar and Fire Control Systems:** Radars, Fire control systems, Transportable Precision Approach Radar (TPAR), Airborne surveillance radars, Maritime radar applications, Drone detection / counter-drone systems
- **Avionics and Electronic Warfare:** Electronic Warfare suites, Self-protection jammer pods, Avionics systems, Electronic support systems, Advanced surveillance solutions
- **Communication Systems:** Communication equipment
- **Satellite Systems:** Satellite systems (under development)
- **Automatic Test Equipment:** Automatic Test Equipment
- **Service and others:** Repairs, overhaul and job work

- Services ~38% of current order book / ~INR350cr (AMC, multi-year; billed as performed, so no receivable build-up).
- Largest Q4 order: IMD radar development + service order (~18-month execution).

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body:
- Revenue growth ~20–25% over short term; mgmt believes actual will be "substantially higher" if repeat/export orders land early.
- EBITDA margin 38–40%; remain net cash / debt-free.
- Cash conversion cycle targeted to settle at ~320–340 days (from 365).
- Aspiration: build order book of ≥3 years' revenue for predictable growth; scale to multi-thousand-crore over 2–3 years.

growth_optionality.title: Growth
growth_optionality.body: Drivers: indigenisation/import substitution, geopolitical defence-capex supercycle (domestic + Europe/UK/US/Japan/Korea exports), repeat orders on accepted products, new product repurposing (anti-drone detection/spoofing/jamming — quick, low-hanging), and seekers/airborne radar/EW programs. AMCA RFP expected "any time now."

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Rising defence spending, increasing indigenisation, growing demand for advanced electronics and expanding global opportunities cited as key growth drivers going forward
- Growing participation of private industry and increasing government defence allocations under Aatmanirbhar Bharat create what management calls a 'once-in-a-generation opportunity' for Indian defence technology companies
- Order inflow growth attributed to diversified wins across multiple defence and aerospace programmes, reflecting growing customer confidence in the Company's technological capabilities and execution track record
- Growing acceptance of the Company's capabilities in international markets, with increasing interest from customers outside India as global defence spending and armed-forces modernisation rise
- Multiple in-house R&D programmes (electronic warfare suites incl. self-protection jammer pods, airborne surveillance radars, maritime applications, drone detection/counter-drone technologies, electronic support systems) have reached advanced stages of development and validation, positioned as the next phase of growth
- All-time high order book in the Company's history as of FY26 year-end
- Order inflows of approximately Rs 1,121 crore recorded during FY26, representing growth of 216% year-on-year, diversified across multiple defence and aerospace programmes
- Export order book of approximately Rs 53 crore as on date, with continued repeat business from the United Kingdom and active engagement with customers across Europe and other international markets
- Successful development, export and acceptance of the Transportable Precision Approach Radar (TPAR) by a European customer marked as an important export milestone

margins.title: Margins
margins.body: FY26 EBITDA 40% (gross 63%). Q4 spike (EBITDA 56%, gross 73%) driven by 100% in-house full-system deliveries with zero bought-out content; weaker quarters reflect strategic low-margin contracts taken deliberately to build full-system/PMO/mechanical capability. Mgmt warns against contract-by-contract margin extrapolation; structural guide is 38–40%.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt-free, net-cash; no leverage taken. Cash deployed into R&D (expensed), capacity expansion and new-product development. No buyback/dividend commentary this call. Focus on improving working-capital cycle.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY26 was described by management as a year of 'historic, tangible expansions' in capability and infrastructure, following a year of vision-setting. The Company continued to build out its Siruseri, Chennai campus, including an EMI-EMC Testing Facility funded from QIP proceeds (against an object of Rs 15.23 Cr, Rs 13.63 Cr had been utilised and Rs 1.60 Cr remained unutilised as at March 31, 2026). QIP proceeds earmarked for product development (Rs 167.24 Cr object) had Rs 131.19 Cr utilised and Rs 36.05 Cr unutilised as at the same date, continuing investment in Radar, Electronic Warfare, Communication and Satellite product lines. Management also referenced 'upcoming infrastructure expansion' built on strengthened internal processes and governance to support the Company's next phase of growth, though no additional named site or capacity project beyond the EMI-EMC facility was disclosed in the routed text.

management_tone.title: Mgmt tone
management_tone.body: Highly bullish and expansive — MD explicitly gave a "first time all-rounded view" on market, investment and scaling, repeatedly stressing growth "substantially higher than guidance" and a multi-thousand-crore ambition. Defensive/irritable on analyst mischaracterisations (denied any "delays" or "poor execution"; insisted execution is fast and good, delays are government-side). Conservative on giving hard timelines/revenue for unproven programs.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Strong reputation for delivering high-quality products and services in Defence and aerospace sectors
- Robust domain capability in Radars, Electronic Warfare, Communication systems, Avionics & Satellite Systems
- Significant, sustained investment in R&D allowing continuous innovation ahead of market trends
- Strong internal quality process and quality team
- Scalable business model with potential to build complete systems
- Deep technical expertise in electronic systems design, embedded software development and manufacturing
- Senior personnel associated with the Company for more than two decades, indicating institutional continuity
- Philosophy of investing ahead of opportunities, so products are already developed and validated before programmes are launched by customers

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- Order timing entirely dependent on government/agency approval cycles (HAL, DRDO, MoD) — lumpy, unpredictable.
- Revenue back-ending / quarterly volatility (Q4 −13% YoY despite strong FY).
- Long working-capital cycle (365 days).
- Margin variability from strategic low-margin contracts.
- Execution/air-trial timelines for EW & new radars (1.5–2 yrs); BrahMos seeker production timing (mgmt downplays risk).
- DRDO gating of missile/seeker programs; capex stranded if contracts slip.
- Competition from foreign OEMs and domestic peers (e.g., Astra Microwave moving into systems).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious
non_obvious.body:
- "Virupaksha" radar (Super Sukhoi) is a DRDO project, NOT a Data Patterns product — mgmt corrected analyst; DPIL has its own equivalent it expects IAF to adopt later.
- Q4 high margin is a mix artifact (no bought-out), not a new run-rate.
- INR1,900cr repeat pipeline is OUTSIDE the INR2,062cr order book and OUTSIDE guidance — large optionality.
- EW self-protection jammer pods already received by IAF, poised for flight testing → medium-term revenue.
- Pursuing electro-optic seekers via an industry partner; wants to become an "electro-optics" not just electronics company.
- Services billed only as performed → does not inflate receivables despite rising services mix.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log
qoq_log.body:
First tracked file for DATAPATTNS (no prior summary in repo). Key Q4 FY26 / FY26 markers vs prior commentary referenced on call:
- Order inflow FY26 ~INR1,121cr, +216% YoY — step-change vs FY25.
- Negotiated-order bucket grew from ~INR1,000cr (prior call) to ~INR1,090cr; some converted; total order book now ~INR2,062cr.
- Q4 revenue −13% YoY but +99% QoQ; FY26 less back-ended (37% in Q4 vs 55% in FY25).
- Cash conversion cycle improved to 365 days (from 428); now targeting 320–340.
- New disclosures: ~INR1,900cr single-vendor repeat pipeline; EW jammer pods accepted by IAF and heading to flight test; AMCA RFP "any time now"; anti-drone product suite entering demos; nine-floor factory expansion underway.
